summary: The only proposal, a $15 SAM buy, puts about 2.4% of equity into its own stop. It takes cash from 13.8% to about 11.4%, which stays above the 10% buffer, and changes the 10% stress loss only a little, from -$23.97 to about -$23.56. The real concern is that it raises the Consumer Staples bucket from 13.9% to about 16.3% two sessions before WMT's confirmed 11-19 print. If you count DPZ by its screen label as the earlier PM decisions did, the Staples stack is about 27.7%. No lesson's applies_to names the Implicator, and I have no graded calls yet. Following L3's caveat, I used `bucket` for the sector claims and gave the label stack only as context.

checks.concentration: SAM goes from 0 to about $15, or 2.40% of $624.32 equity. That is far under the 15% cap and the $65.77 buy cap. The largest single-name weights stay the same: VOO 13.42%, DPZ 11.38%, VTI 10.09%. By bucket, Consumer Staples rises from 13.90% to about 16.30%: WMT 8.05%, KR 5.85%, SAM 2.40%. That makes Staples the largest sector bucket, behind only the US broad equity ETFs at 23.51%; Health Care is 12.77%. Asset-class mix after the trade: single stocks about 62.7% to 65.1% of equity, equity ETFs (VOO and VTI) unchanged at 23.5%, bond and gold ETFs 0%, crypto 0% against the 5% cap, and cash about 13.8% to 11.4%. Cash stays above the 10% buffer (about $62.43), at about $71.02 against $62.43. The book now holds no bond or gold sleeve, so every dollar added is equity risk. SAM's -0.27 beta is the only offset, and it is statistical.
checks.overlap: SAM adds to the Staples factor bet the book already leans on. WMT and KR are held, and earlier runs saw them move together on down days (11-03, 11-06). By SIC label, DPZ (11.38%, Consumer Discretionary by bucket) is also Staples, which puts the label stack at about 27.7%. Single-name business overlap is low, because SAM is a brewer and not a grocer or mass retailer. Timing overlap is the issue: WMT (8.05%) reports on the confirmed date 11-19 and has an unread 11-16 8-K 5.02, so the Staples bucket will be at its largest exactly when WMT's gap risk lands. As a mid-cap, SAM could only be a negligible weight inside VTI, and S&P 500 membership is not in the inputs, so I can't confirm or rule out VOO overlap. The trade does not add to the SPY-200-day shared stop (L9), which still covers VOO and VTI together at 23.51%.
checks.tax: This is a buy, so no lots are sold and nothing is realized. The new lot would open 2026-11-17 and turn long-term on about 2027-11-18. If the $205 stop trips, any loss would be short-term.
checks.wash_sale: none: SAM is not in recent_realized or buy_blocked, and SAM has not been sold at a loss in the last 30 days.
checks.summary: It is small and has its own stop, so it is acceptable at $15. But it pushes the Staples bucket to about 16.3% right before WMT's 11-19 print, so it should not be sized up. SAM's negative beta (+$0.41 in the stress test) probably overstates the protection, because its 0.383 vol is higher than WMT's (0.270) and KR's (0.301).
